newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Quebrada Blanca running close to capacity.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Quebrada Blanca running close to capacity.

text.p: Canadian-owned Quebrada Blanca copper mine in northern Chile will produce around 69,000 tonnes of fine copper cathodes this year -- coming close to design capacity over two years after starting up, said an official.
"We're not at 100 percent yet, but will finish the year working at 100 percent capacity," the mine's general manager James Drake told Reuters.
The mine, which cast its first copper cathode in August 1994, is designed to produce 75,000 tonnes of copper a year when running at full tilt.
Vancouver-based Cominco Ltd, Cominco Resources and Teck Resources International hold a 76.5 percent stake in the mine, built on a remote plateau near the Bolivian border.
Technical problems in adapting heap-leaching technology to the harsh weather conditions at the high-altitude mine slowed startup at the pit, said Drake.

The company installed extra boilers, covered the leach pads with plastic mesh and built hot air ducts within the piles to create warmer conditions for the bacteria which are key to leaching the mine's sulphide ores, he said.
The changes cost Quebrada Blanca $3 million and added two cents a pound to the mine's operating costs, said Drake.
Quebrada Blanca, which has a useful life of 16 years, has cash costs of $0.50 a pound.
